Kakunoori Ramulu vs The State Of Telangana And 5 Others on 7
October, 2025
 1
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal
 Writ Petition Nos.36250, 37238 and 37264 Of 2022
Common Order:

entities.text: Kakunoori Ramulu vs The State Of Telangana And 5 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the issue involved in all these Writ Petitions is one and the same, they are heard together and disposed of by way of a common order.

2. Writ Petition No.36250 of 2022 is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India seeking the following relief/s:-
"...to issue a writ, order or direction, more particularly one in the nature of WRIT OF MANDAMUS, declare the action of the Respondent No.2 to 4 creating government interest over the petitioner land in Sy.No.237/3/A1, Sy.No.237/5/2 to an extent of Ac.2.20 gts., situated at Vuyyalawada Village, Nagarkurnool Mandal, Nagarkurnool District in favour of Government Medical College by way of taking signature on Form No.6  i.e. voluntary surrender of petitioner's land to the government by coercion with a cheating manner as illegal, arbitrary, unjust, violative of principles of natural justice, violative of Articles 14, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India, by holding that the petitioner is the absolute owner and joint possessor in respect of the above said land and consequentially direct the respondents not to dispossess the petitioner from the land in Sy.No.237/3/A1, Sy.No.237/5/2 to an extent of Ac.2.20 gts., situated at Vuyyalawada Village, Nagarkurnool Mandal, Nagarkurnool District and to pass such other and further order or orders..."
3.

Writ Petition No.37238 of 2022 is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India seeking the following relief/s:-
"...to issue a writ, order or direction, more particularly one in the nature of WRIT OF MANDAMUS, declare the action of the Respondent No.2 to 4 creating government interest over the petitioner land in Sy.No.237/17/AA to an extent of Ac.2.20 gts.,
situated at Vuyyalawada Village, Nagarkurnool Mandal, Nagarkurnool District in favour of Government Medical College by taking signature on Form No.6  i.e.
voluntary surrender of petitioner's land to the government by coercion with a cheating manner as illegal, arbitrary, unjust, violative of principles of natural justice,
violative of Articles 14, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India, by holding that the petitioner is the absolute owner and possessor in respect of the above said land and Kakunoori Ramulu vs The State Of Telangana And 5 Others on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193739544/
1 consequentially direct the respondents not to inaugurate the Medical College till compensation, damages paid to the petitioner and further direct the respondent No.1 to initiate penal proceedings under coercion cheating with a criminal conspiracy and SC & ST (POA) Act against the Respondent No.2 to 6 and to pass such other and further order or orders ..."

4. Writ Petition No.37264 of 2022 is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India seeking the following relief/s:-
"...to issue a writ, order or direction, more particularly one in the nature of WRIT OF MANDAMUS, declare the action of the Respondent No.2 to 4 creating government interest over the petitioner land in Sy.No.237/3/A1, Sy.No.237/5/2 to an extent of Ac.2.20 gts., situated at Vuyyalawada Village, Nagarkurnool Mandal, Nagarkurnool District in favour of Government Medical College by way of taking signature on Form No.6  i.e. voluntary surrender of petitioner's land to the government by coercion with a cheating manner as illegal, arbitrary, unjust, violative of principles of natural justice, violative of Articles 14, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India, by holding that the petitioner is the absolute owner and joint possessor in respect of the above said land and consequentially direct the respondents not to dispossess the petitioner from the land in Sy.No.237/3/A1, Sy.No.237/5/2 to an extent of Ac.2.20 gts., situated at Vuyyalawada Village, Nagarkurnool Mandal, Nagarkurnool District and to pass such other and further order or orders..."
For the sake of convenience, the facts in W.P.No.36250 of 2022 are discussed as hereunder:-
5.

Heard Mr.M.Rameshwar Rao, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr.H.Rakesh Kumar,
learned Assistant Government Pleader representing learned Government Pleader for Revenue appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 4.
6.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the official and unofficial respondents colluded with each other and hatched a plan to grab the petitioner's land by inducing him of schemes i.e.,
Dalitha Bandu Scheme, Employment Scheme etc., in the name of construction of Medical College and obtained his signatures on several documents, without paying any compensation as required under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 2013.

Relying on the decision passed by the erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh in LAO-cum-Revenue Divisional Officer Vs. Mekala Pandu And Others 1, wherein it is held that the assignees of the Government lands are entitled to payment of compensation equivalent to the full market value of the land and other benefits on par with full owners of the land, even in cases where the assigned lands are taken possession of by the State, in accordance with the terms of grant or patta, though such resumption is for public purpose, he seeks to allow the Writ Petition.

entities.text: LAO-cum-Revenue Divisional Officer Vs. Mekala Pandu And Others 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue submits that the petitioner had executed a relinquishment deed and also signed on Panchanama, wherein the possession of the subject land was handed over to respondent authorities for construction of the Medical College; that after being Kakunoori Ramulu vs The State Of Telangana And 5 Others on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193739544/
2 satisfied by the voluntary declaration made by the persons concerned and after due identification by the attesting witnesses of Form-C, the said relinquishment was accepted and the subject land was handed over to the authorities for construction of Medical College; that the present construction work was under progress.

sentences.text: Therefore, he AIR 2004 AP 250 states that the said acquisition of land was meant for the larger interest of the public.
Therefore, the claim of the petitioner, at this stage, is perverse and seeks to dismiss the Writ Petition.

8. For better understanding Para No.91 of the decision cited (supra) is extracted as hereunder:-
"Para No.91: 'No compensation' clause which virtually enables the State to withdraw the privilege granted without payment of just compensation is an "unconstitutional condition" imposed by the State
adversely affects the life, liberty, equality and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution.
The assignment of lands to the exploited and vulnerable sections of the society is neither a formality nor a gratis.
The privilege granted is with a view to ensure and protect the rights of the exploited sections of the people to live with human dignity free from exploitation.
The privilege or largess once granted acquires the status of vested interest.

The policy to assign the Government land by the State was obviously designed to protect the socio-economic status of a vulnerable citizenry; its deprivation would be universally perceived as a misfortune".

9. As per the contentions of the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue it is an admitted fact that no compensation was paid to the petitioner in respect of the patta land of the petitioner,
though he has executed various documents.

10. Having regard to the submissions of both the learned counsel and upon careful scrutiny of the decision cited (supra), it is an admitted fact that the Government has acquired the assigned land of the petitioner for public purpose i.e., for construction of Medical College.

Having acquired the subject land of the petitioner, he cannot be deprived of compensation/monetary benefit for acquisition of the subject land, as per the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 2013.

Therefore,
this Court is inclined to direct the petitioner to file a representation along with all the requisite documents, before the respondent authorities seeking compensation in respect of the subject land acquired by them, within four (4) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Upon filing the said representation, the respondent authorities are directed to consider the same and pass appropriate orders, as per law, as expeditiously as possible.
11. With the above direction, these Writ Petition Nos.36250, 37238 and 37264 of 2022 are allowed.
No costs.
Miscellaneous Petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
